app.name: Health monitor
app.tagline: Diagnostics for any platform that speaks the protocol

status.help: Every server or sender that reports its state. Last seen is when its latest heartbeat arrived, re-read here every 10 seconds; one silent for longer than the alert rules allow (Servers not reporting, 5 minutes by default) is shown as down and raises an alert. Packets / min is everything that server sent in the last complete minute, by the name in its packets; the Packets received chart shows it over time.

phase.heading: Phase 0 — scaffold
phase.body: The intake, charts, alerts and search arrive in the next phases.

settings.sound: Play a sound on new alerts
settings.message: Send a message to everyone watching
settings.displaysHelp: A screen with no one at it: a TV or spare monitor showing one dashboard all day. Its link logs itself in, so nobody types a password after a reboot, and it can only watch — no search, no silencing, no changes. Name the screen, pick the dashboard it shows, and point the screen at the link.
settings.noDashboards: This platform defines no dashboards yet, so there is nothing to point a screen at. Add platforms/<platform>/dashboards.yaml first.
settings.tokenOnce: Copy this now: it is not shown again
settings.viewersHelp: Every page with the monitor open right now, wall displays included: one row per browser tab or screen, gone when it is closed. Viewer is the login, or the wall display's name. Since is when that page connected, Last active when it last spoke to the monitor (every 30 s while open), and Updates how many chart updates the monitor has sent it.
settings.visitsHelp: Who had the monitor open, one row per browser tab or wall screen, from when it opened to when it closed. A connection that drops and comes back within 5 minutes (a network blip, a laptop waking up, the monitor restarting) stays the same row and counts as a reconnect. Updates counts only what was sent while the page was connected; the watched charts are all those it asked for during the visit. Kept for data.viewer_history_keep_days (30 days).
settings.noVisits: Nobody had the monitor open that day

chart.partial: Grouping covers only part of the window

criteria.groupHistoryKept_one: Tiles are kept for the last {{count}} minute
criteria.groupHistoryKept_other: Tiles are kept for the last {{count}} minutes; older ones stay empty

connection.lastUpdateAt: Last message from the server at {{at}}

saved.name: Name
saved.copySetLink: Copy a link to this saved set
saved.copyChartLink: Copy a link to these filters

alerts.showingHistory: Showing the alerts recorded on {{day}}. The live window is a separate view.
alerts.historyCapped: Only the latest {{limit}} of that day are loaded; narrow it with the filters or export it as CSV.

silence.title: Silence
silence.reasonHelp: Required: someone will read this in a month
silence.effect: Hidden from the list, with no sound or notification, now and from then on. Still recorded: tick Show silenced on the Alerts tab to see them.
silence.byHelp: Leave empty to use the name you logged in with.
silence.matchHelp: Cut it down to the part that stays the same, e.g. without times or counts. Case does not matter.

maintenance.review: {{count}} mute(s) have been in force for over a month — worth a look

rules.defaultMsHelp: Alert when a request is slower than this
rules.offlineAfterHelp: How long something may stay silent
rules.previewTitle: What these rules would have done in the last {{minutes}} minutes
rules.stepDefault: General threshold: any request, or any signal that reports a duration, slower than this raises a warning.
rules.stepAdd: For URLs that need a different limit, press Add override.
rules.stepMatch: Choose how it matches the URL: Exact path (/api/orders/export), Prefix, for every URL starting with it (/api/reports/), or Glob (/api/*/search; * is one path segment, ** any number).
rules.stepLimit: Set its limit in ms, or tick Never alert for URLs that are slow on purpose.
rules.stepTest: Test against the last hour shows what the rules would have raised; Save rules applies them at once.
rules.stepOrder: When several match, the most specific wins: exact path, then the longest prefix, then the first glob.
rules.fileOnly: The rules file can also set an alert level per rule, narrow a rule to one account, user or server, and mute phrases.
rules.silenceSectionHelp: Alerts to hide: by a part of their message or by category. Hidden alerts are still recorded; Show silenced on the Alerts tab shows them.
rules.latencySectionHelp: When a request, or anything else that reports a duration, is slow enough to raise an alert.
rules.remindEveryHelp: While still down, the same alert again; 0 alerts once

health.kernelDrops: The kernel dropped {{count}} datagrams before the process saw them — raise net.core.rmem_max on the host

reasons.no_adapter: Legacy packet with no adapter for its platform
reasons.adapter_error: Legacy packet the adapter could not read
reasons.intake_tooNew: Packets stamped in the future (sender clock ahead)
reasons.intake_truncated: Datagrams over max_packet_bytes, cut short and dropped (send big messages in chunks)
reasons.intake_chunksDropped: Chunk parts refused (too big, too many, or reassembly memory full)
reasons.alertWriter_errors: Alert history rows failed to write

search.fieldsFound: Fields in these results, click to add
search.addFieldHelp: Any property of the rows, e.g. ipAddress or your own

history.backupHelp: Writes a consistent copy on the server, next to the database or where data.backup_dir in config.yaml says. It stays there; download it below to keep it elsewhere.
history.deleteBackupConfirm: Delete {{file}} from the server? This cannot be undone, and any copy you downloaded is unaffected.
history.backupLimit: Up to {{limit}} backups are kept. Download what you need and delete one to make a new backup.
history.activity: Active users of the monitored application on {{day}}
history.activityHelp: From that day's logs: every account and user the monitored servers reported in requests and other logs. Events less than 10 minutes apart count as one stretch of activity; a lone event counts as a minute. People using this monitor are under Status → Who is watching.
history.backingUp: Writing the backup; on a large database this takes a while…
history.archiveHelp: Move this day out of the database into gzip files now, instead of when it ages out. It can still be downloaded, but not searched.
history.deleteDayConfirm: Delete every log of {{day}} from the database, without archiving it? This cannot be undone. Type the day to confirm.
history.archivesHelp: Days past their time in the database, kept as gzipped JSON, one row per line. Each file is deleted automatically once its day is older than the configured archive period.
history.deleteArchiveConfirm: Delete {{file}} from the server? This cannot be undone.
history.freeSize: {{size}} of it freed, not yet returned to the disk
history.reclaim: Return free space to the disk
history.reclaiming: Returning free space to the disk…

login.name: Your name
login.nameHelp: Only used to label you in the sessions list
login.unreachable: The monitor could not be reached to check your session.

display.diskLow: Disk almost full on the monitor: {{free}} free of {{total}}

dashboard.name: Name
dashboard.title: Title (optional)
dashboard.shipped: From the platform's dashboards.yaml; duplicate it to change it
dashboard.needsPanels: Every row needs a column, every column a panel, and the dashboard at least one row.
dashboard.dragColumn: Drag to move this column, within the row or into another
dashboard.dragPanel: Drag onto another panel or into a column
dashboard.filterHelp: Comma-separated, case-insensitive. The main chart counts only what it keeps.
dashboard.filterHereHelp: Filters this chart for you only, until you leave the page. Comma-separated, case-insensitive.
dashboard.topHelp: Tiles drawn, most active first. Empty draws only 4; the rest are left out, filter or not.

picker.label: Charts
picker.empty: Nothing picked yet. Use the Charts menu to choose which charts and current values to show — the ones you leave out are not collected or sent.

designer.waitingHelp: Signals arriving that the catalogue does not know yet, recognised by their name on this platform: the signal field of a v1 packet, the logPrefix of a legacy customLog, the type of a legacy gauge (jobQueuesLoad, vpnUsersLoad), or the type of any other legacy packet the monitor does not read, which arrives as an alert until an info signal names it. A name no signal is defined for is listed here. A metric or a gauge is not charted until it has a definition; a log is stored and searchable anyway, as config.yaml says, and a definition only names it or gives it its own days. The monitor's own logs (dailyLogs, sendLogs) are not listed: config.yaml sets their days. Remove takes off one that was sent by mistake; it is listed again if it arrives again.
designer.noneWaiting: Nothing is waiting: every signal arriving has a definition.
designer.confirmDelete: Delete the signal {{name}}? Its charts stop; data already stored stays until retention removes it.
designer.saved: {{name}} is defined. It charts from the next packet on; open the Charts tab to see it.
designer.name: Name
designer.nameHelp: The signal name the packets carry
designer.dimsHelp: The fields to group and filter by. Untick one to ignore it; more dimensions means more keys kept in memory.
designer.ttlHelp: 0 uses the server default of two minutes
designer.previewHelp: Drawn from the {{count}} packets held so far, with the mapping above.
designer.badName: A name starts with a letter and holds only letters, digits, '.', '-' and '_'.
designer.emptyDim: Every kept dimension needs a field name.
designer.badRetention: Totals in memory must be at least as long as detail in memory.
designer.detailDaysHelp: After that, per-value rows are summed per hour
designer.keepPairsHelp: Charts split by these two dimensions have history even for times nobody was looking. Other pairs are stored only while a chart shows them.
designer.logRetention: How long its days are kept
designer.logRetentionHelp: Each day of this log is kept in the database (searchable on the Search tab), then as a gzip file on the Storage tab. These override data.log_keep_days and data.log_archive_keep_days in config.yaml for this kind.
designer.archiveDaysHelp: Counted from when the file is written. 0: delete instead of archiving. Empty: as config.yaml says
designer.badLogDays: Days must be whole numbers, or empty
designer.infoHelp: Keeps each packet of one type whole, as it arrived, to read on the Info tab: the latest from each sender and the ones before it. Each sender also shows on the Status tab, and goes down when its reports stop.
designer.packetTypeHelp: The type field as the sender sends it, e.g. configServerJobsListStatus
designer.metricPacketTypeHelp: Optional. A legacy packet type the monitor does not read itself (e.g. ksefEventStatusData): its top-level fields become the dimensions and values below.
designer.colorsHelp: Draw a value in the same colour wherever it appears, e.g. COMPLETED always green, whichever dimension the chart is grouped by.
designer.badColor: Each colour needs a value and a colour like #2e7d32
designer.versionsHelp: The oldest goes when a new one arrives
designer.infoDaysHelp: A sender that stops sending is removed after this many days
designer.noPacketType: Name the packet type to keep
designer.badInfoRetention: Keep at least one report, for at least one day
designer.mergeHelp: Keeps one record per sender and folds every report into it: fields inside objects are merged at every depth, anything else is replaced by the newest, and nothing is removed. Suits a sender that sometimes sends everything and sometimes one part, like the config server's jobsStatusMap. Unticked, each report is kept whole, the newest few per sender.
designer.onStatusHelp: Each sender gets a row on the Status tab and an offline alert when its reports stop for longer than Servers not reporting allows on the Alert rules tab. Untick it for a report sent rarely, like once a day, which would otherwise be taken for a sender gone offline; saving then removes the signal's rows from the Status tab.
designer.logStored: Stored and searchable already; define it to name it or give it its own days
designer.removed: {{name}} removed. It is listed again if it arrives again.
designer.confirmRemove: Remove {{name}} from this list? What was gathered about it is forgotten; it is listed again if it arrives again.
designer.confirmRemoveLog: Remove {{name}} and delete every stored day of it, today included? Its rows cannot be searched afterwards.
designer.infoWaiting: A legacy packet type nothing reads, arriving as an alert; define it as an info signal to keep it as a report. Fields: {{fields}}
designer.logDaysDefault_one: Empty: {{count}} day, as config.yaml says (today and yesterday)
designer.logDaysDefault_other: Empty: {{count}} days, as config.yaml says (today and {{count}} before it)
designer.archiveDaysDefault_one: Counted from when the file is written; 0 deletes instead of archiving. Empty: {{count}} day, as config.yaml says
designer.archiveDaysDefault_other: Counted from when the file is written; 0 deletes instead of archiving. Empty: {{count}} days, as config.yaml says
designer.archiveDaysDefaultDrop: Counted from when the file is written; 0 deletes instead of archiving. Empty: not archived, deleted after its days in the database, as config.yaml says

server.title: This server
server.packetsTrend: Packets per second over the last hour
server.logsDetail: Rows written to the database in the last complete minute, every kind together
server.diskDetail: of {{total}}, holding the {{folders}}; the monitor alerts below data.min_free_gb

storage.keptThenArchived: kept in the database for {{db}} days (searchable), then as gzip files, each deleted {{archive}} days after it is written.
storage.keptThenDropped: kept in the database for {{db}} days, then deleted.
storage.alertDays: Days of alerts in the database
storage.archiveAlertsHelp: Move this day of alerts into its gzip file now, instead of when it ages out. The Alerts tab can then no longer show that day.
storage.deleteAlertDayConfirm: Delete every alert of {{day}} from the database, without archiving it? This cannot be undone. Type the day to confirm.
storage.diskLow: Disk almost full: {{free}} free of {{total}} (holds the {{folders}}). Delete or archive old days, or free space on the host.
storage.leavesHelp: As config.yaml and the log signals stand now, at the hourly check that first finds it past its days (UTC). Changing the configuration changes these.

hints.dashboard: Saved arrangements of charts, alerts and status for this platform, shared with everyone. Pick one, or make and edit your own.
hints.charts: Every chart the platform's signals provide. Choose which to show, group them and set how far back they go.
hints.alerts: What the rules and the platform raised, newest first. Look back at a past day, export, or silence one.
hints.status: Which servers and senders are up, what the monitor itself is using, and who is watching now.
hints.search: Search the stored logs by kind, account, user, URL or text, across the days still in the database.
hints.activity: Who used the monitored platform on a day and for how long, from that day's logs. Not the people using this monitor.
hints.rules: Rules that hide alerts (silences) and rules that raise them: how slow a request may be, and how long a server may stay quiet.
hints.signals: What the platform sends. Define signals that arrive undefined, and edit the ones made here.
hints.storage: What the database and archive files take on disk. Archive or delete past days, and back up the database.
hints.settings: Language, theme and notifications for this browser, a message to everyone watching, and wall-display tokens.
hints.health: The monitor's own problems: packets it could not place, decode errors and dropped writes.
hints.info: Whole reports some senders send, such as the config server's list of jobs: the latest from each sender and the ones before it. Define which packet types to keep as info signals on the Signals tab.

info.none: No reports kept yet. Add an info signal on the Signals tab naming the packet type to keep; its next packet shows up here.
info.undefined: No info signal is defined for these reports any more; they are removed after 30 days.
info.searchHelp: Shows only the fields whose name or value contains this
info.merged: Merged from every report this sender sent: each field shows the latest value it was given.
info.confirmRemove: Delete every kept report of {{signal}} from {{sender}}, and its row on the Status tab? If it is still defined and the sender reports again, it comes back.

packets.title: Received packets
packets.help: Every datagram the monitor receives while this window is open, as it arrived, newest first, up to {{keep}}. Nothing is written to disk: the monitor only keeps them in memory while someone watches, and lets go of them shortly after the window closes. Pick a row to read the packet.
packets.cut: Only the first {{kept}} of {{size}} bytes are kept.
